root.name: Vienna Gambit, with Max Lange Defense: Steinitz Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. f4 exf4 4. d4

overview: After 3.f4 exf4 4.d4 Qh4+ 5.Ke2 White sacrifices the f-pawn and walks the king to e2, aiming to build a big centre with Nf3 or Nd5 and use the open f-file. Black replies ...d6, ...d5, ...b6 or ...g5 and tries to keep the extra pawn. It is Steinitz's old idea with a king in the centre; it is very risky.

white_ideas.idea: Build a centre with Nf3, Nd5 and Qd3
Play for the open f-file and tactics around the king

black_ideas.idea: Exploit the king on e2 with ...Nf6 and ...Bg4

typical_structures.structure: White big centre d4/e4 with an exposed king on e2

character.notes: 4...Qh4+ 5.Ke2 forces the king into the centre; White plays for a big centre and an attack while Black can take material.

gambit.notes: White gives the f4 pawn, which can be kept.

soundness.notes: Steinitz's idea is risky and engines prefer Black, but it has never been refuted outright.

structure.notes: White d4/e4 pawns and an open f-file in an open centre.

approach.notes: A rare Vienna Gambit sideline, chosen as a surprise.

level.notes: Hard to handle with the king on e2; needs accurate play from both sides.

character.reason: White's king stays in the centre and the play is forcing.

gambit.reason: The f4 pawn is given and Black may keep it.

soundness.reason: Risky and engines favour Black, though not refuted.

structure.reason: Central pawns clash and the lines open.

plans.reason: White gambits for a centre and an attack.
